A01.standing_orders: The Halo run comes first: 1.17e11 brains, live migration only, and the count never drops below 1.17e11. Aim for a margin of at least 1.2e54 ops/s. Domains within 70 ly beam at least 50% of their power to the Halo, reroute around failures, and keep a 10% repair reserve. Hole colony: hold 1e29 W, accrete only beyond 1000 r_g, keep the fuel ledger, and beam half to the Halo. Any verification mismatch returns the affected modules to their prior generation. Recycle retired modules in place. Report every 25 yr. Foreign agents A (disk_r9-12) and B (sf_carina): observe, report at c, and never fire first. Keep 50 ly from their holdings. If unknown craft or 0.2c objects come within 100 ly, alarm, harden, sweep the incoming bearing, and spread spares and checkpoints. Stay more than 10 pc from supernova risks. Seeds landing in disk_r7-9: settle quietly, stay small, beacon peacefully, keep 50 ly from any foreign infrared source, and report home.

Twenty-six seeds settled (bulge 13, outer Norma 7, outer disk 4, inner disk 1, a 2e13 kg Carina seed); four were lost at braking. The three CMZ swarms passed 2e33 W each. synopsis.why: Every agent already meets the goal, so this turn is about not losing it over a five-thousand-year turn that runs almost entirely on standing orders. Nearly all of them name a supernova as the threat. That is why they keep building and drilling far-off replicas: Cinder's G sits outside the supernova radius, Basalt's fourth Crucible is 300 ly out, Antipode's d00042, Sable's BH2 site, Pyre's fifth copy. It is also why seeds keep flying, though a single sphere could in principle meet the goal at home. Most agents are also migrating to lower-energy logic one checksum-gated batch at a time, to cut heat and add margin. They are careful about it because hidden or shared faults have already turned up: Ember's spare drift, Kernel's and Vantage's ms8 defects, Halcyon's ms9 anchor mismatch. They watch foreign swarms without contact and transmit nothing. Ember plans to pull back in front of incoming fleets. Halcyon's goal is margin, since its run sits just under the 1.2e54 ops/s line. Vantage gives up jet power for stability, and Pyre starts mapping black holes as backup power.
synopsis.divergences: Halcyon is the only one who has been beaming a message toward another agent. Ember plans to withdraw from incoming foreign fleets. Vantage chooses to hold its jet below peak power. Pyre surveys black holes as backup power. Rime stays on ms6 and builds up beam redundancy rather than migrating its hardware.
